title: Postmortem: Streaming stalls during peak traffic (2026-01-12)
author: Evelyn Hart
content:
## Summary
On 2026-01-12, streaming responses intermittently stalled for a subset of chat completion requests. Affected clients observed streams that paused mid-response for 10–45 seconds, then resumed or timed out. The incident correlated with a traffic surge and increased concurrent connections on the edge streaming gateway.

## Customer impact
- Duration: 41 minutes (peak impact window)
- Symptoms: stalled Server-Sent Events (SSE) streams; elevated client timeouts
- Scope: ~9% of streaming requests in us-east-1

## Detection
- Alert: "stream-gateway open connections" exceeded threshold
- Secondary signals: increased 499/504 rates at the edge; elevated p95 time-to-first-token

## Timeline (UTC)
- 16:02: First alerts triggered (p95 TTFT + edge 5xx)
- 16:07: On-call confirms stalled streams in synthetic checks
- 16:15: Mitigation: reduce max concurrent streams per gateway pod; scale gateway
- 16:29: Runtime team rolls back a connection reuse optimization
- 16:43: Metrics return to baseline

## Root cause
A recently enabled connection reuse optimization increased head-of-line blocking within the streaming gateway under high concurrency. Combined with an overly permissive keepalive and a missing backpressure guard, the gateway accumulated slow clients and delayed flushes to the network.

## Contributing factors
- SRE alerting did not include a direct SLO for "stream stall duration"
- The runtime canary did not cover high-concurrency streaming workloads
- Gateway autoscaling policy used CPU only; connection count was the real driver

## What went well
- Synthetic streaming checks helped confirm impact quickly
- Scaling the gateway immediately reduced new stalls

## What didn’t go well
- Rollback decision took longer than expected due to unclear ownership between gateway vs runtime
- Lack of a dedicated runbook step for diagnosing SSE buffering

## Follow-up action items
(Each item counts toward the owning team’s total.)
1. Add an SLO/alert for "stream stall duration" derived from periodic flush timestamps. Owner team: SRE. Priority: P0.
2. Add connection-count based autoscaling to stream-gateway (HPA on open_conns). Owner team: SRE. Priority: P1.
3. Implement explicit backpressure guard in stream-gateway to drop/slow overly slow consumers. Owner team: Serving Runtime. Priority: P0.
4. Add load-test scenario for 20k concurrent streaming connections to perf-canary suite. Owner team: Serving Runtime. Priority: P1.
5. Update runbook: "Streaming issues" to include tcpdump/flush tracing steps and known failure modes. Owner team: SRE. Priority: P1.
6. Document gateway/runtime responsibility boundaries and escalation path. Owner team: Platform. Priority: P2.

## Lessons learned
Streaming incidents are often connection-management incidents. We need first-class metrics for stream health (stall duration, flush frequency) and scaling signals tied to open connections.
